elements.char: Conclusion
elements.label: text

elements.char: We have presented high quality image samples using diffusion models, and we have found connections
elements.label: text

elements.char: among diffusion models and variational inference for training Markov chains, denoising score
elements.label: text

elements.char: matching and annealed Langevin dynamics (and energy-based models by extension), autoregressive
elements.label: text

elements.char: models, and progressive lossy compression. Since diffusion models seem to have excellent inductive
elements.label: text

elements.char: biases for image data, we look forward to investigating their utility in other data modalities and as
elements.label: text

elements.char: components in other types of generative models and machine learning systems.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Broader Impact
elements.label: text

elements.char: Our work on diffusion models takes on a similar scope as existing work on other types of deep
elements.label: text

elements.char: generative models, such as efforts to improve the sample quality of GANs, flows, autoregressive
elements.label: text

elements.char: models, and so forth. Our paper represents progress in making diffusion models a generally useful
elements.label: text

elements.char: tool in this family of techniques, so it may serve to amplify any impacts that generative models have
elements.label: text

elements.char: had (and will have) on the broader world.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Unfortunately, there are numerous well-known malicious uses of generative models. Sample gen-
elements.label: text

elements.char: eration techniques can be employed to produce fake images and videos of high profile figures for
elements.label: text

elements.char: political purposes. While fake images were manually created long before software tools were avail-
elements.label: text

elements.char: able, generative models such as ours make the process easier. Fortunately, CNN-generated images
elements.label: text

elements.char: currently have subtle flaws that allow detection [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], but improvements in generative models may
elements.label: text

elements.char: make this more difficult. Generative models also reflect the biases in the datasets on which they
elements.label: text

elements.char: are trained. As many large datasets are collected from the internet by automated systems, it can be
elements.label: text

elements.char: difficult to remove these biases, especially when the images are unlabeled. If samples from generative
elements.label: text

elements.char: models trained on these datasets proliferate throughout the internet, then these biases will only be
elements.label: text

elements.char: reinforced further.
elements.label: text

elements.char: On the other hand, diffusion models may be useful for data compression, which, as data becomes
elements.label: text

elements.char: higher resolution and as global internet traffic increases, might be crucial to ensure accessibility of
elements.label: text

elements.char: the internet to wide audiences. Our work might contribute to representation learning on unlabeled
elements.label: text

elements.char: raw data for a large range of downstream tasks, from image classification to reinforcement learning,
elements.label: text

elements.char: and diffusion models might also become viable for creative uses in art, photography, and music.
elements.label: text
